QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Amoxicillin?

RESPONSE:
The excerpt you've provided only covers the Indications and Usage and Dosage and Administration sections for amoxicillin/clavulanate potassium 600 mg/42.9 mg per 5 mL oral suspension — it does not include the Drug Interactions section, so I can't cite interaction information from this label text.

For general context (not drawn from the excerpt above), the full prescribing information for amoxicillin/clavulanate products typically lists interactions such as:

• Probenecid — decreases renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin, raising and prolonging amoxicillin blood levels; co-administration is generally not recommended.
• Oral anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) — abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time/INR has been reported; monitoring is advised when co-administered.
• Allopurinol — concurrent use with amoxicillin may increase the incidence of rash.
• Oral contraceptives — reduced efficacy has been reported with ampicillin-class antibacterials; additional contraceptive measures may be considered.
• Other antibacterials — bacteriostatic agents (e.g., chloramphenicol, macrolides, sulfonamides, tetracyclines) may interfere with the bactericidal effect of penicillins.
• Laboratory test interference — false-positive urine glucose with non-enzymatic (copper reduction) methods; effects on some estriol assays in pregnancy.

Please verify against the complete FDA-approved prescribing information for the specific product, and have a pharmacist or prescriber review the child's full medication list, since this excerpt cannot confirm these details.
